This experience surfaces relevant actions in-context to help users restore site functionality without navigating deep into settings.

title: Microsoft Purview compliance portal: Insider Risk Management: Data Security Investigations integration
description: Launch a pre-scoped Data Security Investigation (DSI) from an IRM case. When a data security admin identifies a risky user who needs deeper investigation, they can launch a pre-scoped investigation directly from an IRM case, allowing them to view content analysis related to that user and better assess post-incident data impact. Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management correlates various signals to identify potential malicious or inadvertent insider risks, such as IP theft, data leakage, and security violations. Insider Risk Management enables customers to create policies based on their own internal policies, governance, and organizational requirements. Built with privacy by design, users are pseudonymized by default, and role-based access controls and audit logs are in place to help ensure user-level privacy.

title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Optional Public CDN Support in Brand Center Setup
description:
We are updating the Brand Center setup experience so that administrators can set up Brand Center without enabling Public CDN.

Today, Public CDN is enabled as part of Brand Center setup, even when an organization only wants to use branding governance capabilities that do not require it. With this update, organizations can begin using Brand Center while deferring Public CDN until they need capabilities that depend on it, such as organizational fonts.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Manage rental service demand with work order requests
description:
Rental organizations need to coordinate commercial rental activity, equipment availability, asset condition, and service execution across multiple teams and applications. Service needs can arise while equipment is in stock, in transit, at a customer site, or being returned, but those needs don’t always require an immediate work order.

This feature connects rental operations in Dynamics 365 Finance and Supply Chain Management with Dynamics 365 Field Service by introducing fleet items and work order requests for rental service scenarios. Field Service users can view relevant fleet, rental contract, location, movement, and asset information while service needs can be captured and reviewed before a work order is created.

Work order requests provide a controlled intake and approval process, allowing teams to validate service needs before committing technicians, inventory, or scheduling resources. When approved, a request can create a Field Service work order while preserving the relevant fleet item, asset, and rental context as the work progresses.

This connected experience gives rental, service, and operations teams better visibility and coordination across the rental service lifecycle while giving organizations greater control over when service work is initiated. The capability can be used with Field Service alone or with the combined Field Service and Project Operations solution.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Book Work Orders with Multiple Requirements
description:
Dispatchers can now select which resource requirement to schedule when booking a work order that has multiple requirements. The new Book experience is available from both the work order form and list view, and shows relevant details such as requirement duration, time windows, resource preferences, booking status, and links to active bookings.

Work orders with a single resource requirement continue directly to the configured Schedule Assistant or Quick Book experience. The requirement picker is accessible, responsive, localized, and supports right-to-left languages.

title: Microsoft Teams: Customize blocked file extensions for Weaponizable File Protection
description: Microsoft Teams is expanding admin controls for Weaponizable File Protection. Administrators will be able to customize which file types are blocked in Teams to align with their organization's security requirements or continue using the Microsoft-recommended default list. This added flexibility helps organizations tailor file protection policies while maintaining a secure collaboration environment.

title: Microsoft Edge: Ask Copilot about an image
description: Ask Copilot about an image in Edge enables users to instantly analyze images from the web by sending them directly to Copilot from the Edge context menu, making it easy to ask questions, gain insights, and understand visual content without leaving their browsing experience. Admins can control availability to this feature using the EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext and Microsoft365CopilotChatIconEnabled policies.

title: Microsoft Edge: Enhanced Autofill
description: For desktop users, Microsoft Edge can now autofill additional document types—including passports, driver’s licenses, and other specialized forms—on top of your saved addresses.

title: Outlook: Multi Account Search
description: Users will be able to see results from multiple mailboxes interweaved in a single ranked list and will be able to do standard mail actions.

title: Dynamics 365 Finance: Core finance - Improve financial journal processing and control
description:
Finance teams rely on journals for high-volume accounting processes, where performance, accuracy, and visibility are critical to keeping financial operations moving. The new financial journal capabilities in Dynamics 365 Finance will provide a more scalable approach to creating, importing, reviewing, and posting journals, helping finance teams reduce manual steps and identify issues earlier in the process.

Finance teams can work with customer and ledger account types, import journals and review errors without navigating to the Data management workspace, and preview intercompany and intracompany accounting, accruals, and allocations before posting. Related documents make it easier to trace transactions, while integration with advanced tax calculations supports applicable tax scenarios. Future-period accruals no longer post automatically, reducing the need to keep future periods open.

Optimized financial dimensions and the Ledger posting rules framework are prerequisites for using these capabilities.

title: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Copilot Cowork for Government Clouds
description: Copilot Cowork makes it easy to delegate work. Describe the outcome you want and Cowork automatically grounds the work in your emails, meetings, messages, files, and data.

title: Planner: Expiration of plans from meetings due to inactivity
description: Planner plans created from Teams meetings (via Meeting Notes or Loop) often remain unused long after the meeting ends. These inactive plans accumulate and clutter over time. This feature automatically expires and deletes meeting-created plans that have had no task activity for 180 days. Only the Planner plan is removed whereas the tasks in Loop and meeting notes stay intact.

title: Microsoft Edge: Autolaunch opt-in experience for managed devices
description: Microsoft Edge will introduce an opt-in experience that allows users on managed devices to choose whether Edge launches automatically when Windows starts. Administrators can also manage this behavior through the LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled policy with opt-in, opt-out, and user-choice configurations.

title: Microsoft Purview: Data Lifecycle Management-Legacy Teams retention policies covering Copilot will be treated as Teams-only
description: Some existing retention policies scoped to Microsoft Teams may currently also apply to Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions. As part of an upcoming change, these legacy Teams retention policies will be converted to—and treated as—Teams-only policies. They will no longer implicitly govern Copilot workloads.

title: Microsoft Purview: Unified Classification Management Experience
description: The Unified Classification Management Experience unifies every classifier in Microsoft Purview—Sensitive Information Types (SITs), Exact Data Match (EDM), fingerprint SITs, and trainable classifiers—into one place to discover, create, validate, and manage classifiers.

title: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Edit your document with Copilot in PowerPoint in Government Clouds
description: Copilot in PowerPoint helps you create, edit, and refine presentations through natural language—right inside your deck. Start a new presentation or build on an existing one by asking Copilot to generate slides, update content, improve layouts, and polish design, all while preserving your formatting, structure, and branding. Copilot can also connect to your brand kit to apply branded templates, insert brand-approved images, and check for brand compliance. Available to Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) users.

title: Endpoint Data Loss Prevention — Endpoint DLP now supports a pre curated list of file extensions for the file extension condition
description: Endpoint DLP now includes a pre curated list of file extensions for the file extension condition. Previously, file extensions were entered as free form text, which could result in unsupported or non-scannable extensions being used. This could lead to gaps in protection and increase processing overhead on endpoints. With the pre curated list, you can select only supported file extensions. This helps improve policy reliability and reduces unnecessary processing on endpoints.

title: Microsoft Teams: Intelligent recap for DoD
description: Intelligent meeting recap uses AI to provide a quick summary of your meeting, highlighting key discussion points, identifying follow-up actions, and offering quick access to significant points such as name mentions, when a screen was shared, individualized speaker markers, topics, and chapters.

title: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Realtime voice interactions in Word and PowerPoint
description: Use your voice to talk with Copilot, interact in-real time, and understand the content within your document or presentation. Updated September 9, 2026: We will be re-releasing this feature with updates in October. Thank you for your patience.

title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Quality evaluation supports knowledge source in criteria
description: Criteria questions can now use knowledge sources to help evaluate customer interactions. This allows organizations to ground evaluation criteria in approved knowledge content, policies, or guidance so quality checks can better reflect expected handling standards. This preview capability is scoped to case and on-demand evaluations.

title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Inactivate quality evaluation records
description: Quality managers can now inactivate evaluation records that should no longer contribute to scoring or reporting. Inactive evaluations are preserved for traceability but excluded from overall score calculations and analytics. This helps teams correct reporting outcomes when evaluations were created in error, used the wrong criteria, were duplicates, or should otherwise be removed from active quality results.

title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Support Not Applicable answer option for quality evaluation criteria
description: Criteria questions now support a Not Applicable answer option. When a question is marked as not applicable, it is excluded from scoring instead of negatively affecting the evaluation score. This helps ensure evaluations remain accurate when a specific criterion does not apply to the case, interaction, or business scenario being reviewed.

title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Detailed quality evaluation score breakdown
description: Evaluation details now include a scoring breakdown at the overall, section, and question level. Users can see how the final evaluation score was calculated, including how individual question outcomes contribute to section scores and the overall score. This improves transparency, helps quality teams validate results, and makes it easier to identify areas for coaching, calibration, and process improvement.

title: Microsoft Viva: Ability for leaders to publish Power BI reports
description: Microsoft Viva Insights is extending its report publishing capabilities from analysts to leader personas such as Chief Officers, Managers and their delegates. This enhancement enables leaders to directly distribute curated reports within their organizations through a lightweight publishing experience, complementing the existing report customization features.

title: Microsoft Teams: Events in Meet app in Teams in GCC High and DoD
description: Users can now use the Teams Meet app to discover events across their organization, track what important events are upcoming, and plan and organize their own professional events. With this release, Meet app will be renamed to Events app.

title: Microsoft Purview: Data Lifecycle Management - Ensure regulatory compliance by deleting inactive OneDrives and mailboxes for departing employees
description: Enables admins to delete both content and containers for departed users at scale thereby keeping your tenant compliant without any manual effort.

title: Microsoft Purview: eDiscovery - In-product diagnostics to troubleshoot common challenges
description: Self-service diagnostics help identify common issues with case permissions, security filters, and policy status. The experience highlights potential misconfigurations and provides simple guidance to help customers understand and resolve them. This brings basic troubleshooting into the product and helps eDiscovery admins overcome common challenges.

title: Microsoft Purview: Data Lifecycle Management - Insights and policy recommendations on sensitive M365 data for better Data Security and Compliance posture
description: Insights on sensitive M365 data (OneDrive and SharePoint) and recommendations on retention policies for customers to better govern their sensitive data.

title: SharePoint: eSignature for Microsoft 365 - Recipient groups
description: Recipient groups in eSignature allow a recipient slot to be assigned to multiple people, such that any one  of those people can fulfil the signing requirement on behalf of the group.

title: Microsoft Purview: Data Loss Prevention– Unmanaged cloud app discovery and protection with Microsoft Purview and the Island Enterprise Browser
description: Microsoft Purview network data security now integrates with Island, extending protection to Island’s browser-based workflows at the point of user interaction. With this integration, new and existing Island customers can configure Microsoft Purview collection and data loss prevention policies to detect and protect data shared with unmanaged cloud apps through the Island Enterprise Browser, the Island Extension, and browser add ins via HTTP and HTTPS, using the same classifiers, sensitive information types, and sensitivity labels used in other Purview policies. Island provides visibility and control at the presentation layer, including typed and pasted input, file transfers, and extension activity, so data can be inspected before it ever leaves the browser. This integration further enriches Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM), Insider Risk Management (IRM) risk score, enables data security and compliance for AI interactions, and more.

title: OneDrive: Improved max path error experience on desktop
description: OneDrive desktop sync users now get clearer, more actionable guidance when file paths exceed the supported 520-character limit. The updated experience shows exactly how many characters a path is over the limit and offers a guided flow to rename or move the affected items so they can sync.

title: Dynamics 365 Project Operations: Transaction Journals
description:
Transaction journals let users author complete time, expense, and material transactions—including different transaction classes within the same journal. Users enter transactions through a dedicated Transactions tab and select Preview to generate and review the journal lines and relationships that will be created.

When the journal is confirmed, Project Operations creates the applicable cost, unbilled-sales, and inter-organizational actuals, along with the required relationships between them, without creating an approval record or initiating an approval workflow. The confirmed journal is then locked using the existing journal behavior, and resulting actuals can be corrected through the existing correction-journal process.

title: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Federated Copilot Connectors will support write, update and delete actions
description: Federated Copilot connectors (MCP type) currently let Microsoft 365 Copilot read data from third-party services in real time. With this update, the connector tools that create, update, and delete content in those services are unblocked in Copilot Chat, so users can complete work without leaving Copilot. Copilot acts with the user's own account and permissions at the third-party service, and every create, update, or delete action requires the user's explicit confirmation before it runs. Admins can view each connector's read and write/delete tools in the Microsoft 365 admin center and disable connectors that don't meet their organization's policies.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Choose how work order services flow into project financials
description: Organizations can now control how work order services contribute to project financials when using Dynamics 365 Field Service and Project Operations together. A new administrator-level setting lets organizations choose whether work order services flow as time or material transactions based on how they manage field execution and technician labor.

title: Microsoft Teams: Upgraded call history in Teams Calls app
description: Call history in the Teams Calls app is being upgraded to make it easier to find and act on past call activity. Missed calls and associated voicemails will be consolidated into a single call history entry, reducing clutter and simplifying follow-up. Call history will also expand from 100 records to up to 3,000 records or 6 months of history, whichever limit is reached first, giving users more context when they need it.

title: Microsoft Teams: Analytics for desk utilization on Teams Pro Management portal
description: Teams admins can access utilization analytics for Teams bookable desks on Teams Pro Management portal, similar to analytics provided for meeting rooms on the portal today. For utilization analytics to be enabled, a desk needs to have one or more peripheral device associated, and the desk needs to be licensed with Teams Shared Space license or Teams Shared Space - Single Space license.

title: Microsoft Purview: Information Protection-Auto-labeling per-policy coverage report
description: For each enforced auto-labeling policy, admins can view how files processed during enforcement correlate to the latest simulation run. The per-policy coverage report shows volumes of files that have been labeled or are not yet labeled, and whether those files were included in the last simulation snapshot. This helps admins understand enforcement progress for a specific policy against the data state captured during simulation, while also identifying files that were not found in the simulation snapshot but were processed during enforcement.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Optimize asset maintenance schedules using completed service
description:
Business value

Asset maintenance is most effective when service intervals reflect how equipment is actually used and maintained. Static schedules that continue from an assumed date or meter value can cause an organization to service an asset more often than necessary after early maintenance or wait too long after late, partial, or usage-intensive service.

Feeding completed maintenance activities, actual completion dates, and meter readings back into the maintenance plan recalibrates future requirements around the asset's real operating and service history. This closed-loop approach helps organizations avoid both over-maintenance and under-maintenance, balancing asset reliability and availability with labor, parts, and service costs.

Feature detail

Completed maintenance is used as a planning input, not only recorded as service history. When maintenance work is completed, the system evaluates which planned maintenance activities were fulfilled and feeds the actual completion date and relevant meter readings back into the asset's maintenance plan. The plan uses those results as the new basis for calculating the next applicable maintenance requirement.

For calendar-based maintenance, the next event is recalculated from the completed service and the plan's recurrence rules. For usage-based maintenance, the next threshold is calculated from the asset's meter value when the activity was completed. For criteria that combine time and usage, the plan continues to evaluate both conditions from the updated maintenance baseline. Sequential plans advance according to the activities that were actually completed.

The optimized plan then supplies updated due dates and activities to maintenance coverage views, demand forecasts, and future work-order generation. As additional maintenance is completed, the feedback loop keeps the schedule aligned with the asset's evolving usage and service history.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Forecast planned maintenance demand
description:
Business value

Maintenance demand often becomes visible to service operations only after work orders are created, leaving limited time to prepare capacity and materials. A forward-looking maintenance forecast gives organizations earlier visibility into expected work so they can anticipate labor, skills, parts, and scheduling demand across the asset population.

This supports more proactive operational planning and helps teams identify periods of concentrated demand before they result in resource conflicts, parts shortages, or delayed maintenance.

Feature detail

Provide a forecast of maintenance events expected within a selected future planning horizon. Bring together events calculated from calendar schedules, actual meter usage, sequential maintenance plans, and projected usage based on meter history.

Allow planners to understand when maintenance is expected and which assets, plans, and activities contribute to the forecast. Expected activity duration and other planning information from the maintenance definition can be used to represent the likely operational demand.

The forecast provides visibility before work orders are generated. As schedules, meter readings, and usage predictions change, the expected maintenance demand can be refreshed to reflect the latest plan.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Forecast asset usage to predict maintenance due dates
description:
Business value

Usage-based maintenance aligns service with the work an asset has actually performed, but a current meter reading alone does not tell the organization when the next threshold will be reached. Forecasting the asset's expected usage rate converts meter-based maintenance from a reactive trigger into a forward-looking planning signal.

Maintenance and reliability teams can use the projected due date to plan labor, parts, capacity, and customer downtime before the threshold is reached. Because the estimate is derived from the individual asset's recent operating history, it reflects real utilization more closely than a generic calendar assumption while remaining explainable and reviewable by planners.

Feature detail

Calculate a projected usage rate for each asset from the trailing 30-day mean of its historical meter-usage logs. This rate represents the asset's recent pace of operation and drives all projected due dates for usage-based maintenance activities on that asset.

For each usage-based maintenance requirement, use the calculated rate to translate the remaining usage before the next threshold into an estimated calendar due date. The configured meter threshold remains the maintenance requirement; the projected date provides the advance planning signal used by maintenance forecasts and lead-window work-order generation.

Store the calculated usage rate and the date and time when it was last calculated. Exposing both values lets planners assess how fresh the estimate is and whether the available history is sufficient to rely on the projection.

Apply outlier protection when calculating the trailing mean so isolated meter spikes, incorrect readings, or other anomalous input data do not disproportionately change the projected usage rate. Recalculate the rate as additional meter history becomes available so future maintenance predictions continue to reflect the asset's recent usage.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Plan asset maintenance using time, actual usage, and service sequences
description:
Business value

Organizations can maintain assets according to how the equipment ages, how much it is actually used, and which service activities have already been completed. A flexible maintenance schedule helps avoid servicing lightly used equipment too often while reducing the risk that heavily used equipment operates beyond its required maintenance interval.

Usage-based schedules connect maintenance directly to meter readings recorded for the individual asset. This allows work to be driven by actual operating hours, mileage, cycles, production counts, or another tracked measure rather than by an estimated calendar interval alone. Combining scheduling methods in one plan supports more consistent execution of manufacturer guidance, internal reliability standards, and contractual maintenance commitments.

Feature detail

Define maintenance activities against the actual usage of an asset by specifying recurring service intervals on its meter. For example, require an oil change after every 150 operating hours or an inspection after every configured number of miles, cycles, or units produced. As new readings are recorded, the asset's accumulated usage determines when the next maintenance interval is reached.

Define other activities using calendar recurrence or combine calendar and usage criteria in one rule. For combined criteria, the plan initiates maintenance when either the elapsed-time threshold or the actual-usage threshold occurs first.

Create sequential maintenance programs in which different activities become due at different points in the maintenance cycle. For example, a plan can progress through inspections, minor services, major services, and overhauls rather than repeating the same activity at every interval.

The maintenance plan continuously evaluates its configured intervals against the asset's dates, recorded meter usage, and completed maintenance sequence to determine which activity is due next. When the applicable threshold is reached, the plan produces the maintenance requirement that drives downstream work-order generation. This gives planners one place to manage calendar-based, actual-usage-based, whichever-comes-first, and multi-step maintenance strategies.

title: PowerPoint: Skills in Brand Kit
description: Upload skill (.md file) in Brand Kit and use within PPT Copilot

title: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Local inferencing
description:
Local inferencing expands Microsoft Copilot’s sovereign controls by enabling AI inferencing for supported Copilot interactions to occur within the applicable local geography.

Launching in Australia, India, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom, and the United States, this capability gives organizations greater control over where AI inferencing occurs, helping them address sovereignty and regional requirements. Inferencing is the processing step when an AI model executes a prompt to produce an output or response.

title: Microsoft Teams: Additional health signals available for Teams Rooms on Android on Pro Management Portal
description: Expanded Pro Management Portal (PMP) health monitoring for Teams Rooms on Android by surfacing device health signals including storage health, Teams meeting app, calendar sync, secondary display health and network. When issues are detected, PMP will automatically generate actionable alerts and support ticket creation workflows, enabling IT administrators to proactively identify and triage room health issues before they impact meeting experiences.

title: Outlook: Insert Symbol
description: You can insert a variety of symbols into an email message while composing it. To add a symbol, go to the Insert tab and select Symbols.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Process subcontractor photos, completion documents, and inspection results
description:
Business value

Subcontractors often document completed work through photos, service reports, inspection forms, certificates, and other files. When those documents remain only in a shared mailbox, service teams must manually download, interpret, organize, and reconnect them with the work they support. Important completion evidence and inspection findings can be difficult to find when a customer, dispatcher, auditor, or future technician needs them.

Processing subcontractor completion documents as part of the closeout keeps evidence and supported findings connected to the Field Service work. This improves traceability, reduces document-handling effort, and preserves a more complete operational history.

Feature detail

The Subcontractor Agent processes supported attachments received with a subcontractor submission, including photos, PDFs, service reports, inspection documents, and other supported completion files. It associates those files with the relevant Field Service work so authorized users can find the evidence from the operational record rather than searching the mailbox.

The agent can use supported document content when preparing the closeout proposal. For an inspection or task-completion document, this can include extracting supported inspection findings, outcomes, observations, deficiencies, or task results for the internal reviewer to validate and apply to the appropriate Field Service record.

The review experience keeps the original document available alongside the proposed structured information so the dispatcher, service coordinator, or other authorized reviewer can compare the extraction with the source. Unsupported, unreadable, encrypted, oversized, or potentially unsafe files are surfaced for appropriate handling instead of being represented as successfully processed.

Processing an invoice, parts list, or other financial or consumption document does not by itself create, match, approve, or post a financial transaction or product-consumption record unless that behavior is separately supported.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Close out bookings and work orders from subcontractor service reports
description:
Business value

Subcontractors commonly communicate completion through an emailed service report or a message describing the work performed. Dispatchers then have to find the correct assignment, interpret the report, update the booking and work order, and copy important closeout details into Field Service. This manual process delays operational visibility, creates inconsistent service history, and can leave completed bookings or work orders open.

Using the subcontractor's service report to prepare the complete closeout gives service teams a faster and more consistent way to reconcile external work. Booking state, work-order status, and the details of the completed visit can be reviewed together before the internal records are updated.

Feature detail

The Subcontractor Agent processes a supported email and service report, identifies the applicable Field Service work order and active booking, and prepares a coordinated closeout proposal.

The proposal can include supported booking and work-order status changes together with completion details extracted from the submission, such as the completion summary, work performed, notes, recommendations, requirements, requested follow-up, actual completion information, and supported labor-duration values.

An internal dispatcher or service coordinator reviews the source submission and the proposed values, corrects or selects the supported changes as allowed, and deliberately applies them to Field Service. Coordinating the booking and work-order changes keeps scheduling records, operational status, and service history aligned.

If the sender is not authorized, the work cannot be matched confidently, multiple bookings could apply, required information is missing, or the message contains no actionable closeout information, the submission is routed for human resolution rather than being silently applied.

This feature closes out existing supported bookings and work orders. It does not create new follow-up work, process payroll or invoices, or automatically create parts and product-consumption records unless those capabilities are delivered separately.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Onboard mid-lifecycle assets into maintenance plans
description:
Business value

Organizations often introduce maintenance management after equipment is already operating or acquire used assets with established age, usage, and service histories. Starting those assets at the beginning of a new maintenance plan produces irrelevant past activities and inaccurate future dates, while manually reconstructing every historical event requires significant effort.

Mid-lifecycle onboarding allows existing assets to enter a standardized maintenance program at an appropriate point, helping organizations expand maintenance coverage without treating every asset as newly commissioned.

Feature detail

Apply a reusable maintenance plan template to an existing or used asset and initialize the resulting plan using the asset's current lifecycle information. Relevant inputs can include commissioning or installation date, current meter usage, known maintenance history, and the appropriate position in a sequential maintenance program.

Advance through earlier template activities that no longer apply so the asset begins with the next relevant maintenance requirement. Preserve the context used during initialization so planners can understand how the starting position was determined.

After initialization, the asset participates in the same scheduling, forecasting, work-order generation, completion feedback, and coverage experiences as other assets using the maintenance plan.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Review and visualize an asset's maintenance schedules
description:
Business value

An asset can have several lines of service, each with its own maintenance schedule, recurrence pattern, and future events. When those schedules are reviewed separately, planners have difficulty understanding the asset's complete maintenance plan and how the different service requirements will play out together.

A consolidated list and visual timeline give maintenance teams one place to understand the asset's planned service, investigate individual events, and identify schedules or timing that should be adjusted. This visibility supports faster, more informed planning without requiring teams to reconstruct the plan from separate records.

Feature detail

From an asset's maintenance plan, view all maintenance schedules for that asset in one place. Review each line of service and the schedule that controls when its maintenance activities become due, including calendar-based, usage-based, combined time-and-usage, and sequential criteria.

Visualize how those schedules are expected to play out over time. The visualization brings the projected maintenance events from the asset's schedules into a chronological view so users can see how the different service lines relate to one another and when maintenance is expected.

Users can select and investigate an individual maintenance event to understand the service activity, schedule, trigger, and expected timing behind it. They can then return to the relevant schedule when its criteria, recurrence, sequence, or timing needs to be changed.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Create and apply reusable maintenance plans to assets
description:
Business value

Organizations can define a consistent maintenance strategy once and use it across groups of similar assets instead of designing a separate plan for every asset. This reduces setup effort, limits configuration differences across locations and teams, and provides a repeatable way to bring growing asset populations under managed maintenance.

Reusable templates also make maintenance standards easier to govern. Asset and service leaders can establish the expected maintenance program for an equipment type while allowing each asset to have the plan it needs for ongoing execution.

Feature detail

Create maintenance plan templates that describe the maintenance program for an asset model, manufacturer, product, SKU, or asset category. A template brings together the maintenance activities and scheduling rules that should apply to that type of equipment.

Use a template to establish a maintenance plan for one or more eligible customer assets. The resulting asset maintenance plan provides the asset-specific context used to schedule activities, forecast maintenance, and generate future work.

The template and assignment experience helps users identify the appropriate standard for an asset and consistently establish maintenance coverage without rebuilding the complete maintenance definition each time.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Enhanced visibility into work order financial performance
description:
The new Work Order Cost Summary gives field teams a clearer view of how project-related work is performing by bringing estimated and actual costs, sales, and project task progress together in one place. Teams can quickly compare what was planned with what was actually delivered across products, services, and expenses.

When the Work Order is associated with a Project Task, the summary also shows planned and completed task effort, allowing users to review financial performance and execution progress together.

The summary recalculates automatically as the Work Order moves through key execution statuses, including Scheduled, In Progress, and Completed. Users can also select Refresh Totals at any time to recalculate the summary and review the latest Work Order and project values.

By bringing Field Service execution data together with Project Operations financial and task information directly on the Work Order, teams can identify cost and execution variances earlier, make more informed decisions while work is in progress, and reduce the need to manually reconcile information across applications.

This feature is available when the Field Service and Project Operations integration is enabled.

title: Microsoft Teams: Schedule Channel Meetings from Outlook Calendar
description: Users will be able to schedule Microsoft Teams channel meetings directly from Outlook Calendar. This streamlines meeting creation and helps keep discussions and meeting content connected in the appropriate channel.

title: Microsoft Teams: Schedule Teams Channel Meeting from Win32
description: Users can now schedule Teams Channel Meetings from Win32 (Outlook classic client)

title: Microsoft Purview: DSPM-Copilot Readiness and Data Explorer
description:
We’re introducing the new readiness for Microsoft Copilot and data explorer experiences in Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM). These new capabilities provide data security teams with greater visibility into their organization’s data security posture and help them assess risks, investigate findings, and prioritize remediation.

The readiness for Microsoft Copilot experience in Purview DSPM helps organizations assess and improve their data readiness for Microsoft Copilot. It brings together insights into sensitive data exposure, oversharing, and protection coverage, helping security teams identify risks and assess progress toward a more secure Microsoft Copilot deployment.

The new data explorer experience in Purview DSPM provides a centralized investigation experience that helps organizations understand where sensitive data exists across sites, review site-level access, and explore relevant data through preset views. It brings together sites, sensitive data, and preset views, to support more efficient investigations and reduce context switching.

title: OneNote: Multimodal capture in Copilot Notebooks (Windows)
description: Capture on Windows helps you bring conversations and ideas from meetings, brainstorming sessions, and everyday work into Copilot Notebooks. Capture audio, images, and notes in one experience, then let Copilot turn them into structured notes with key insights, decisions, and action items, in a Copilot Notebook of your choice

title:
Microsoft Teams: AI-powered notes for in-person
meetings with Facilitator in Teams Rooms on Android
description: In addition to capturing real-time notes and meeting outcomes during scheduled or hybrid meetings, the Facilitator agent assists you with notes, decisions and actions for in-person meetings in Teams Rooms on Android. Simply invite Facilitator with one tap of the room console. Meeting notes appear on the front of room display or touch board, are available via meeting recap when shared, and deleted if no one selected. Rest assured no data remains in the room. Available with Teams Rooms Pro.

title: Microsoft Power Platform governance and administration: Maker Guidelines
description:
The Maker guidelines feature gives organizations a direct way to share guidance with Copilot Studio makers in the flow of work. Administrators can explain which tools, models, connectors, and channels are approved for an environment and point makers to the right policy, request process, or support contact.

The message appears in the Review pane alongside the agent's blockers and warnings and remains available when the agent has no issues. This gives makers a consistent place to understand organizational expectations and find help without leaving Copilot Studio.
products: Microsoft Power Platform governance and administration

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Support multiple payers across Work Order lines
description:
Field work does not always have a single payer. A customer may be responsible for the primary service while another party, such as a warranty provider, manufacturer, partner, or other eligible billing customer, is responsible for specific products or services performed during the same visit.

This capability gives service teams more flexibility during execution by allowing the billing responsibility to be determined at the individual Work Order line level rather than just requiring every transaction on the Work Order to follow the same payer.

title: PowerPoint: Async Notifications for Copilot in PowerPoint
description: Enable users to leave PowerPoint, switch devices, go offline, or end their workday while remaining confident that Copilot will notify them when work is complete or requires attention.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Expand your service offering through subcontractors without the onboarding overhead
description:
Business value

Subcontractors commonly communicate completion through an emailed service report or a message describing the work performed. Dispatchers then have to find the correct assignment, interpret the report, update the booking and work order, and copy important closeout details into Field Service. This manual process delays operational visibility, creates inconsistent service history, and can leave completed bookings or work orders open.

Service teams can setup an agent to process subcontractor service reports to prepare a coordinated booking and work-order closeout. This supports faster reconciliation of external work and helps keep scheduling status, operational records, and service history consistent.

Feature detail

An agent in Dynamics 365 Field Service processes supported emails and service reports, identifies the applicable Field Service work order and active booking, and prepares a coordinated closeout proposal.

The proposal can include supported booking and work-order status changes together with completion details extracted from the submission, such as the completion summary, work performed, notes, recommendations, requirements, requested follow-up, actual completion information, and supported labor-duration values.

An internal dispatcher or service coordinator reviews the source submission and the proposed values, corrects or selects the supported changes as allowed, and applies them to Field Service. Coordinating the booking and work-order changes keeps scheduling records, operational status, and service history aligned.

If the sender is not authorized, the work cannot be matched confidently, multiple bookings could apply, required information is missing, or the message contains no actionable closeout information, the submission is routed for human resolution rather than being silently applied.

This feature closes out existing supported bookings and work orders. It does not create new follow-up work, process payroll or invoices, or automatically create parts and product-consumption records unless those capabilities are delivered separately.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Support multiple warehouse assignments for field technicians
description:
Field technicians often source parts from more than one warehouse. Limiting a technician to a single warehouse can make it harder to reflect how materials are actually sourced across field operations.

With this capability, administrators can assign multiple warehouses to a Bookable Resource and designate a preferred/default warehouse for the applicable legal entity. When a technician records material consumption, the warehouse can be automatically populated based on the Work Order legal entity and the technician’s configured default warehouse for that legal entity, while still allowing the technician to select another applicable warehouse when needed.

This reduces manual selection for technicians, helps ensure materials are recorded against the correct warehouse and legal entity, and gives organizations more flexibility to reflect how inventory is actually managed across field operations.

This capability is supported in the Integrated deployment type with Project Operations, where Field Service works with Finance and Supply Chain Management through Dual-write.

title: Microsoft Teams: Proximity join support for attendees in Teams events from Teams Rooms on Windows and Android
description: Attendees can take advantage of proximity join with Teams Rooms on Windows and/or Android for fast, effortless connection to nearby room systems during Teams events, such as town halls, webinars, and structured meetings.

title: Microsoft Teams: Enhanced IntelliFrame with AI data channel for intelligent cameras
description: Teams Rooms on Windows users can now benefit from next generation IntelliFrame features on certified AI-capable cameras with on-device video processing. With IntelliFrame’s expanded AI data channel, participants experience faster active speaker framing, people recognition and labels, and more responsive meeting views—even when network conditions are limited. These capabilities are available with Teams Rooms Pro.

title: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Copilot Chat in Outlook expands to reason over inbox, calendar, and enterprise data
description: Copilot Chat in Outlook expanding to support reasoning over a user's entire inbox, calendar and other enterprise data for Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat users (without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license) .

title: Microsoft Teams: New sharing panel in meetings - improved content discovery and ease of sharing
description: The sharing panel in today’s meetings is the default place for content discoverability and sharing. New sharing panel UI is crafted with intent of modernising and simplifying default tasks such as window sharing, but also for easier discovery of sharing options and more discoverable file sharing.

title: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Copilot in SharePoint
description: Simplifies SharePoint content management and ensures content is Copilot-ready by automating metadata, fixing stale content, enabling fast page creation, improving compliance, and enriching content so Copilot can deliver more accurate, grounded answers. Updated April 16: We are still in development for GA and have launched to Preview only.

title: Microsoft Edge: Ground Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in Edge for Business in your open OneDrive and SharePoint documents
description: Get relevant answers and insights about your open cloud documents in Copilot Chat in Edge.

title: Microsoft Purview: Information Protection-Auto-labeling scale increase for SharePoint and OneDrive
description: We are increasing the maximum auto-labeling capacity for SharePoint and OneDrive from 100,000 up to 500,000 files per tenant per day. This helps organizations label and protect more of their data at rest, faster, closing labeling gaps across existing content. With sensitivity labels and protection settings applied to more files sooner, organizations can better prepare their data estate for Microsoft 365 Copilot with greater confidence.

title: OneDrive: Prompt gallery for Copilot
description:
Discover easier ways to use Copilot in OneDrive
The new Prompt Gallery offers ready-to-use prompts for common file tasks, helping you get started quickly, discover what Copilot can do, and customize prompts to fit your needs.

Access the Prompt Gallery from:

The Copilot button in the bottom-right corner of OneDrive
The + button in the Copilot chat pane
Select Open Prompt Gallery to explore prompts across categories such as Create, Analyze, Find, and Collaborate.

title: Microsoft Clipchamp: Copilot video creation updates
description: Copilot brings agentic video creation to Clipchamp Video Hub. Users can generate, edit, and refine videos from prompts—grounded in explicit documents or implicit WorkIQ knowledge. Preview and playback video directly in chat, then continue iterating towards a finished video.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Track costs for non-billable field work
description:
Organizations often use the same field teams for both customer work and internal operational work, such as maintenance, inspections, or asset-related activities that are not billed to an external customer. These scenarios still require scheduling, technician execution, and accurate tracking of the labor, materials, and other costs associated with the work.

With this capability, Field Service Work Orders can be connected to a project that serves as the financial container for the work. Technicians continue to plan and execute through Field Service, while supported labor, material, expense, and other costs are captured against that project for centralized cost tracking.

This gives organizations a consistent way to manage non-billable field work and understand its total cost without requiring a customer contract simply to connect the Work Order to a project.

title: Microsoft Teams: Granular Conditional Access for Teams meetings
description: Granular Conditional Access for Teams meetings gives organizations greater control over access to sensitive meetings. Administrators can apply Conditional Access policies to selected meetings, helping ensure participants meet organizational security requirements before joining.

title: Microsoft Teams: Multi-line call history tabs in the Calls app
description: Multi-line users get a redesigned call history experience that organizes activity by phone line. Call activity is organized into dedicated tabs for each line, so history, voicemails, and recordings appear under the line they belong to, making navigation and call management simpler and more intuitive.

title: Microsoft Teams: Enable agents for existing applications in your organization
description: For third-party applications already being used in your organization, admins can now discover and enable the corresponding Teams agents from within the Teams Admin Center. Admins receive recommendations for high-value agents and gain visibility into any required configuration changes during the enablement workflow. These agents increase employee productivity by bringing their everyday applications into the flow of work in Teams. This helps organizations get more value from their existing software investments and unlocks more surfaces for the tools their users already rely on.

title: Outlook: New Copilot entry point in Classic Outlook
description: We've introduced a new experience for Copilot in the apps—a consistent entry point across apps that sits above your work and understands the context beneath it. Rather than scattering touchpoints across the interface, it anchors Copilot as one connected system across Microsoft 365, surfacing relevant actions that help you stay in flow. With this release, we are rolling out this new experience - already available across other Outlook endpoints, as well as in Word, Excel and PowerPoint - to classic Outlook.

title: Microsoft Purview Compliance Portal: Information Protection- Scan existing files in SharePoint and OneDrive for business for sensitive information
description: This new capability will enable admins to scan existing files at rest in SharePoint or OneDrive for business for sensitive data.

title: Viva Glint - Action Taking Report (Public Preview)
description: Introduction of a new report that provides transparency into platform activity by dashboard users. Metrics such as report views, Team Conversations completed, and Focus Areas created will be visible and filterable with this report.

title: Microsoft Purview compliance portal: Information Protection - Sensitivity label grouping modernization
description: To help improve label usability and configuration, the sensitivity labeling scheme will be simplified to only consist of labels and label groupings. These new label groupings allow admins to better organize and categorize their labels (previously done via parent labels).

title: Microsoft Copilot Studio: Discover & Add Skills from the skill catalog
description: With the Skills catalog in Copilot Studio, makers can discover, reuse and selectively share approved organizational skills instead of recreating the same instructions and workflows for every agent. The shared catalog powered by Microsoft 365 App Store enables shared skills to extend across experiences such as Copilot Studio M365 copilot, and Cowork, helping organizations standardize proven ways of working while maintaining centralized governance.

title: Work IQ: ExpandedContextIQ
description: Expand Context IQ so users can discover and select additional agents, skills, and content sources while composing prompts.

title: Work IQ: Custom agents + 3P calls
description: Enable Work IQ to invoke custom agents and agents that call supported third-party tools.

title: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft M365): Delegated prompt publishing for organization prompts
description: This release follows the availability of organization prompts, providing admins the ability to upload custom prompts for their organization in the Copilot app home screen. Now, admins can delegate organization prompt publishing to users, AAD security groups, and distribution groups. These delegated users and groups will be able to create, edit and delete organization prompts at the tenant level through the Prompt Lab, without having to access the Microsoft 365 Admin Center. Admins can continue to monitor and provide oversight through the current experience in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center.

title: Microsoft Purview: Data Loss Prevention - Data Security for non-Microsoft connected apps
description: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention and Information Protection Auto-labeling capabilities now extend to non-Microsoft connected apps (e.g., Google Workspace, Box, Dropbox, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Amazon Web Services, and Cisco Webex). The conditions and actions supported for each of these applications vary.

title: Microsoft Teams: Personal message reminders for chat and channels
description: Teams now lets you set and manage reminders directly on chat and channel messages, helping you keep track of important items. Create, update, complete, and delete reminders, track them in a dedicated Reminders view, and receive timely notifications when they become due. Reminders are private to each user and include message context, making them easy to revisit and act on when needed.

title: Microsoft Purview: Insider Risk Management – Policy Recommendation Panel in IRM
description:
Today, Insider Risk Management (IRM) provides policy-driven protection for data leaks, data theft, and risky AI usage. However, while policy-driven protections are powerful, customers may not always have clear visibility into where coverage can be optimized or expanded to address latent insider risk.

IRM now provides guidance on what protections are missing or which policy configurations deliver the most incremental value, providing customers with more comprehensive coverage to mitigate their most critical insider risk.

Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management correlates various signals to identify potential malicious or inadvertent insider risks, such as IP theft, data leakage, and security violations. Insider Risk Management enables customers to create policies based on their own internal policies, governance, and organizational requirements. Built with privacy by design, users are pseudonymized by default, and role-based access controls and audit logs are in place to help ensure user-level privacy.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Finance - Use withholding taxes (WHT) with employee transactions
description:
This feature extends withholding tax capabilities to include employee transactions. The feature supports scenarios where employee-related payments or reimbursements are subject to withholding tax requirements and ensures that you accurately process the transactions in the financial system. Key capabilities include:

  • Apply withholding tax rules to employee transactions.
  • Automatically calculate withholding tax amounts based on configured tax setups.
  • Maintain consistent tax treatment across vendor and employee transaction processing.

When someone creates an employee transaction, the system finds the applicable withholding tax configuration and applies the relevant withholding tax treatment. This capabililty enables organizations to meet local tax requirements for employee-related payments while keeping financial records accurate and compliant.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Finance - Vendor specific number series for Self-billing Invoices
description:
Organizations that use self-billing often need to follow supplier-specific invoicing requirements, including unique numbering conventions. With this enhancement, users can define and assign dedicated number series for self-billed purchase invoices on a per-vendor basis.

Key capabilities include:

  • Set up a unique number series for individual vendors that participate in self-billing arrangements.
  • Automatically apply the vendor-specific number series when creating self-billed purchase invoices.
  • Maintain separate invoice numbering sequences across different suppliers.
  • Improve compliance with vendor agreements and local business requirements that mandate specific invoice numbering practices.
  • Reduce manual intervention and the risk of numbering errors during invoice generation.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Finance - Calculate multiple excise duties per item
description:
This feature enhances excise tax management by allowing multiple excise duty definitions to be associated with a single item and calculated during transactions.

Key capabilities include:

  • Assign multiple excise duty configurations to the same inventory item (i.e, item is liable for both plastic and sugar tax).
  • Automatically calculate all applicable excise duties during purchasing and vendor-related transactions.
  • Support complex tax scenarios where products are subject to more than one excise levy.
  • Reduce the need for manual workarounds, customizations, or separate item records to represent different tax obligations.
  • Improve tax accuracy and consistency across purchasing, inventory valuation, and financial reporting processes.

With this enhancement, businesses can model real-world excise tax structures more effectively while maintaining compliance with local regulatory requirements. The system aggregates and applies all configured excise duties for an item, ensuring that tax amounts are calculated consistently and transparently throughout the transaction lifecycle.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: E-Documents - Exchange EDI documents
description:
This feature extends the E-Documents framework to support Electronic Data Interchange (EDI), which enables organizations to exchange business documents electronically with vendors and partners using widely adopted industry standards. Key capabilities include:

  • Leverage the existing E-Documents framework as a unified platform for managing electronic document exchange.
  • Enable organizations to send and receive structured business documents without relying on paper-based or manual processes.
  • Exchange documents using Peppol BIS 3, which is an often used for electronic procurement and invoicing, but also opened for adding new formats based on local or customer standards.
  • Support order exchange, and sending remitannce advices, and is open for additional document types.
  • Facilitate standardized document exchange between organizations and vendors.
  • Automate the generation, transmission, and processing of electronic business documents.
  • Align with regulatory, industry, and partner requirements for electronic document exchange.

By bringing EDI capabilities into e-documents, organizations can modernize their supply chain and procurement processes while using a consistent, scalable approach to electronic business communication.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Expense Agent - Calculate withholding tax automatically in expense reports
description:
Organizations can automatically calculate employee withholding taxes (WHT) as part of the expense report process. When employees submit expenses that are subject to withholding tax requirements, the system applies the appropriate tax calculations directly within the expense report workflow. Key capabilities include:

  • Automatic withholding tax calculation for employee expense transactions that require tax deductions.
  • Calculate single or multiple withholding taxes for each category, based on you setup. Calculations can also be simple or compound.
  • Calculate thresholds based on different periods for records, documents, categories (period accumulation), and total (period accumulation).
  • Base calculations on gross or net amounts.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Expense Agent - Calculate and report VAT based on expense reports
description:
Expense Agent supports automated VAT handling for expense reports, which can help simplify tax management and improve reporting accuracy. Key capabilities include:

  • Automatic VAT Calculation: Expense Agent identifies VAT-relevant expense transactions and calculates applicable VAT amounts based on the information in submitted expense reports.
  • VAT-Aware Expense Processing: VAT values are incorporated into the expense review and processing workflow, reducing the need for manual tax calculations.
  • Enhanced VAT Reporting: VAT amounts captured from employee expenses are aggregated and reported, supporting financial reporting and tax recovery processes.
  • Improved Compliance: Standardized VAT handling helps ensure that expense-related tax calculations apply consistently across the organization.
  • Human in the loop: If the VAT calculation is enabled for expense reports, accountants must review VAT calculation and confirm that everything is correct before posting it.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Expense Agent - Use assigned projects only in the web app
description:
Expense Agent web app now uses dedicated resource assignments for projects to determine which projects are available to each user when they create or manage expense entries. Key capabilities include:

  • You can assign dedicated resources (employees) to the whole project or to the specific task.
  • Display only projects or/and tasks where the user is assigned as a resource.
  • Automatically filter project lists based on project-resource relationships.
  • Reduce the risk of users selecting projects that aren't relevant to their role or assignments.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Expense Agent - Improve duplicates prevention
description:
Expense Agent can identify and handle duplicated expense submissions. Key capabilities include:

  • Enhanced duplicate detection that identifies expenses with matching or highly similar details, such as amount, date, merchant, receipt, or transaction information.
  • Proactive guidance that alerts employees when it detects a potential duplicate expense in the current expense report, or one that is already posted.
  • Reduced manual review effort by helping prevent duplicate claims from entering approval and reimbursement workflows.
  • Improved expense data integrity through more intelligent validation and comparison of submitted expenses.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Expense Agent - AI-Driven Approvals
description:
Expense Agent can validate submitted expense reports against approval policies written in natural language and provide approvers with guidance during the review process. After an employee submits an expense report, the system evaluates both the overall report and the individual expense lines to detect potential policy violations, suspicious patterns, or situations that might require closer attention. This process supports policies that aren't limited to exact thresholds or fixed numeric conditions, such as when business class travel is allowed, what qualifies as an appropriate business meal, or when exceptions to preferred hotel standards might be acceptable. The result is additional review context that helps approvers make better-informed decisions without replacing the final human approval step.

By running policy validation after submission, the feature can apply controls at the level of a single expense line in the first release. The feature complements existing approval workflows by highlighting issues, providing context, and helping organizations enforce policy consistently while keeping approvers in control of the final decision.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Expense Agent - Add date ranges and vehicle types in your mileage calculation
description:
Expense Agent now supports advanced mileage rate configuration based on both effective date ranges and vehicle types, enabling more flexible and accurate mileage reimbursement calculations. This enhancement combines mileage rate scheduling with support for differentiated vehicle categories. Key capabilities include additions on the Mileage Rate Setup page:

  • Define mileage rates that are valid only within specific date ranges, allowing organizations to accommodate rate changes over time.
  • Configure separate mileage reimbursement rates for different vehicle types, such as cars, motorcycles, electric vehicles, or other organization-defined vehicle categories.
  • Automatically apply the correct reimbursement rate based on the travel date and selected vehicle type during mileage expense calculation.
  • Support evolving regulatory requirements, company policies, and regional reimbursement standards without requiring manual recalculation of submitted mileage claims.

Administrators can maintain a set of mileage rate records that include both an effective date range and an associated vehicle type. When someone creates a mileage expense, Expense Agent evaluates the trip date and the type of vehicle, and then applies the matching reimbursement rate automatically. This evaluation ensures that mileage claims are calculated using the appropriate rate in effect for the specific travel period and mode of transportation.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Expense Agent - More countries and languages
description: Expense Agent supports more languages and regions, enabling an experience for users in all countries/regions where Business Central is available, and adding the following languages: Czech, Dutch, Finnish, Icelandic, Italian, Norwegian, and Swedish.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Preserve actual booking End Time when completion is recorded later
description:
Business value

Technicians do not always record booking completion at the moment work ends. They may update the booking later because of connectivity, customer-facing responsibilities, or end-of-day administration. When the later administrative action replaces the booking End Time, the recorded duration can extend beyond the work that was actually performed and affect downstream journals, time entries, labor costs, actuals, and work-order completion reporting.

Field Service administrators can choose whether completion by the booked resource automatically changes the booking End Time. Organizations whose technicians complete bookings later can preserve the existing or explicitly supplied work end, helping booking duration and downstream time and cost records remain aligned with when the work occurred.

Feature detail

Use the organization-level Set End Time on booked resource completion setting in Field Service settings to control the automatic End Time update.

  • With the setting set to Yes, which is the default, current behavior is preserved. When the booked resource completes a booking without supplying End Time, Field Service sets End Time to the completion time and recalculates Duration.
  • With the setting set to No, Field Service preserves End Time and Duration when the booked resource completes the booking unless the completion request explicitly supplies a different End Time.
  • Completion by another user or an integration continues to preserve End Time for either setting value.

When the setting is No and the booked resource completes the booking, Field Service uses the retained or supplied End Time as the effective Completed booking timestamp. This keeps timestamp-derived booking journals and automatic time entries aligned with the recorded work end. Dataverse audit fields continue to show when the completion was submitted.

The setting applies to future completion transitions and does not rewrite historical bookings. It does not change the booking-status lifecycle, invoice generation, or the existing Work Order Completed On calculation, which continues to use the latest eligible booking End Time.

title: OneDrive: Updated placement of the Create or upload button for Web
description:
OneDrive for the web is updating the placement of the Create or upload button to provide a more consistent file experience across OneDrive and SharePoint. The button will move from the left navigation pane to the right side of the page, bringing familiar navigation from SharePoint document libraries to OneDrive.

The available options for creating files and folders or uploading content will remain unchanged.

title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Service tools, skills and plugins are now available for Cowork, Code and Scout
description:
The updated Service application brings Dynamics 365 Customer Service context, actions, and guided workflows into supported Copilot experiences, including Chat, Cowork, Code, and Scout. Customer service teams can work with service information and take supported actions in the flow of work, reducing the need to switch to Dynamics 365.

First-party tools delivered through the Service package on Dynamics 365 MCP respect Dynamics 365 business logic and the user's existing permissions on each call. The package provides a governed foundation for the supported tools and skills. Availability is tracked separately for each experience.

title: Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations cross-app: Role-based access controls for ERP agents
description: Dynamics 365 ERP security administrators can apply additional, agent-specific security restrictions that take effect when a user accesses the ERP through an agent. Administrators define these restrictions using the existing security model — assigning roles, duties, and privileges that apply only to agent-initiated requests, scoped by legal entity — so that a user's agent session can operate with narrower permissions than the same user holds when working directly in the ERP.

title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Generate maintenance work orders within a configurable lead window
description:
Business value

Organizations can turn upcoming maintenance requirements into executable Field Service work without requiring planners to monitor every asset and create each work order manually. Generating work at a controlled point before it is due gives dispatchers time to secure technicians, skills, parts, and customer access while avoiding an unnecessarily large backlog of work created too far in advance.

This connects long-range maintenance planning with day-to-day service execution and helps ensure that a valid maintenance requirement becomes actionable at the right time.

Feature detail

Configure a lead window that determines how far in advance an upcoming maintenance event should create a work order. When a scheduled or predicted event enters that window, generate the corresponding Field Service work order for the customer asset.

Carry the relevant maintenance context into the generated work, including the maintenance activity and the information required to prepare and schedule service. Depending on the configured maintenance definition, this can include tasks, products, services, required skills, and expected duration.

Work-order generation can operate from maintenance due through calendar recurrence, actual meter usage, or a projected usage date. The generated work remains connected to the originating maintenance event so planners can understand why it was created and prevent duplicate demand.

title: Microsoft Copilot Studio: Self-learning for Copilot Studio Agents
description: Soon agents can help makers improve agents using lessons from completed runs. It will identify repeated tool sequences that can be handled by workflows to standardize agent behavior, minimize errors, and most importantly control costs. Makers will be presented with recommendations and supporting evidence, expected impact, and the related instruction and tool changes. Makers accept recommendations, configure, test, and publish a refined copy of the agent. This helps improve agent output quality and controls costs while preserving work that requires model judgment and keeping makers in control.

title: Microsoft Copilot Studio: Persistent identity for Copilot Studio Agents
description: Makers can now give their Copilot Studio agents their own accounts, making it a governed Microsoft 365 identity for shared, collaborative business processes that spans across teams. With its own mailbox, Teams presence & Office access, the agent can collaborate where work happens while admins can control and govern its access, policies and use as its own first-class entity.

title: Microsoft Teams: Report a Message or an External User for Security Concern in Gov Clouds
description: Users in Gov clouds can now report suspicious messages and external users within Teams. Reports are surfaced in the Teams admin center, giving admins greater visibility into potentially malicious activity and enabling them to investigate and take appropriate action. By incorporating end-user reports as an additional security signal, this capability helps organizations identify and respond more quickly to phishing, impersonation, spam, and other messaging threats.

title: Microsoft Teams: App centric management in Teams Admin Center to manage the Apps access for tenants, end-users, and groups in DoD
description: App centric management introduces new admin settings to control who in the tenant can install Teams apps. First, admins can set a default value for new apps that are published to Teams app store. Second, admins can edit the availability of an app to “All users can install,” “Specific users and groups can install,” or “No user can install.” This feature evolves the existing app permission policies and provides admins with the ability to manage access to the app individually. The app permission policies for existing customers are migrated to maintain existing app availability in the tenant.

title: Microsoft Teams: App centric management in Teams Admin Center to manage the Apps access for tenants, end-users, and groups in GCC High
description: App centric management introduces new admin settings to control who in the tenant can install Teams apps. First, admins can set a default value for new apps that are published to Teams app store. Second, admins can edit the availability of an app to “All users can install,” “Specific users and groups can install,” or “No user can install.” This feature evolves the existing app permission policies and provides admins with the ability to manage access to the app individually. The app permission policies for existing customers are migrated to maintain existing app availability in the tenant.

title: Microsoft Edge: Automatically unsubscribe users from notifications sent by scam and malicious sites
description: Microsoft Edge now helps further protect users from malicious web notifications. When a notification leads users to a site that Microsoft Defender SmartScreen blocks as a scam, phishing, or malware page, Edge automatically stops that source from sending users further notifications and lets users know. Users can review and restore any of these sites anytime under edge://settings/privacy/sitePermissions/allPermissions/notifications.

title: Microsoft Teams: Chat for organizers and presenters in structured meetings and webinars on Teams Rooms on Windows
description: When a Teams Rooms on Windows acts as an organizer, co-organizer or presenter in a structured meeting or webinar, you have access to the private chat for event management known as the Event Group. You can also switch to a separate chat with attendees enabling smooth event experiences for all. Available in Teams Rooms Pro-licensed rooms.

title: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Deep citations in Copilot
description: Deep citations let users quickly verify Copilot's results by linking directly to the relevant part of the reference, boosting trust. We're starting with Word and PPT files, then adding Meetings, Web, and PDF references.

title: OneNote: Summary and Q&A in OneNote Mobile with Copilot (Iphone)
description: With this new Summary feature in OneNote mobile, you can create a short and fluent summary of your longer pages which will help to consume relevant information faster. With the Question and Answer at your fingertips, you can get real-time answers to your queries directly within your notes, enhancing your ability to access and utilize information quickly and effectively.
