title: Dynamics 365 Commerce: Store Commerce - Configure inline actions on transaction line items in Store Commerce
description:
Inline actions extensibility enables retailers and implementation partners to configure the set of actions displayed per line item in the modern transaction grid in Store Commerce, using Screen Layout Designer in Dynamics 365 Commerce headquarters.

What retailers can configure

  • Which actions appear: Select any eligible out-of-the-box POS operation or custom operation registered in headquarters to include as an inline action on transaction line items.
  • Display order: Control the sequence in which inline actions appear, so the most relevant operations for a given store format or associate role are surfaced first.
  • Custom operations: Operations built through the POS extension framework can be added as inline actions alongside out-of-the-box operations, giving retailers a unified configuration surface for both standard and customized workflows.

Default behavior and backward compatibility

No configuration is required to preserve the current experience. If no inline actions are configured for a layout, Store Commerce continues to display the existing default set of inline operations. There is no change in behavior for layouts that haven't been updated. Once a retailer configures inline actions for a specific layout, the configured list replaces the defaults for that layout only. Other layouts remain unaffected.

Localization

  • Out-of-the-box operations: Display names are automatically localized using existing POS resource strings. No additional localization work is required.
  • Custom operations: Display names fall back to the operation name configured in headquarters. Retailers and partners who need localized display names can provide them with the POS extension framework using resource files and operation mappings in their extension code.

Security and permissions

Inline actions respect the same POS security roles and permission model as button grid operations. Retailers can use role-based access controls to restrict sensitive operations, such as price override or void line, to managers, while presenting a simplified action set to cashiers.

Requirements

This feature requires the modern React-based transaction grid. The following feature flags must be enabled in Feature management in Dynamics 365 Commerce headquarters:

  • Modern transaction grid (RetailModernTransactionGridFeature)

The legacy transaction grid doesn't support inline actions extensibility.

How to configure inline actions

  1. In Dynamics 365 Commerce headquarters, go to Retail and Commerce > Channel setup > POS setup > POS > Screen layouts.
  2. Open the screen layout to configure and launch Screen layout designer.
  3. Select the transaction grid component and open the inline actions configuration.
  4. Add operations from the available list, remove operations that aren't needed, and set the display order.
  5. Save the layout and run the Channel configuration distribution schedule (1090) to push the changes to stores.

Changes take effect in Store Commerce after the updated layout is downloaded at the register.

Applies to: Point of sale (Store Commerce)

Business Value:

Retailers adopting the modern transaction grid in Store Commerce have had no control over the inline actions displayed per line item. Operations such as adding a serial number, changing a delivery method, applying a discount, or voiding a line were presented as a fixed, hard-coded set. This is the same for every store, every role, and every layout. There was no way to change this. The inline actions list was not extensible, even with developer involvement. This meant slower rollouts, unnecessary development cycles, and configuration changes that required code when they shouldn't have. For partners and ISVs, the gap was equally sharp. Custom operations they have built for retailers can't surface inline on line items at all, reducing discoverability and forcing associates to hunt through menus for operations that should be one tap away.

Inline actions extensibility removes this cost. Retailers can now select which actions appear per line item, control their order, and include custom operations all through Screen Layout Designer in Dynamics 365 Commerce headquarters. No code, no deployment. Changes are pushed to stores through the standard distribution schedule.

The feature is also risk-free to adopt. Existing deployments continue to show the current default inline actions unchanged. Retailers who configure inline actions for a layout replace the defaults only for that layout, giving them full control over the pace and scope of rollout.

Scenario

With Customer Insights - Data, you can see which contacts opened the email and interacted with your product. When you act on real engagement signals, you refine your audience, increase relevance, and boost sales.

When you create segments in Customer Insights - Data and use them in Customer Insights - Journeys campaigns, the interaction data captured by Customer Insights - Journeys can now be accessed and used in Customer Insights - Data segments to refine your segments based on how customers responded to your campaign. title: Dynamics 365 Commerce: Omnichannel commerce - Enable credit management support for Commerce orders
description:
This feature enhancement extends the standard credit management framework to all Commerce orders across channels, ensuring the consistent application of credit policies between Commerce and Supply Chain Management. During order fulfillment, Commerce channels including call center and POS adhere to defined credit management blocking rules to determine whether an order should be placed on credit hold for review. For order capture scenarios, POS and Commerce e-commerce continue to rely on the existing Check credit limit on sales order configuration in credit and collections parameters to evaluate whether a credit limit check should be performed at order placement.

To use these capabilities, store administrators must enable a new Enable credit management for Commerce orders feature flag in the Commerce headquarters Feature management workspace.

Two exceptions to standard credit limit validation remain in place:

  • Cash-and-carry transactions paid on credit continue to be blocked when the customer’s available credit is insufficient, ensuring that on‑account purchases can't bypass credit policies.
  • Customer orders using a carry-out mode of delivery continue to be marked as Exclude from credit management, because these orders are partially invoiced immediately when the customer pays for items they carry out at the point of sale.

This feature enhancement ensures unified and predictable credit governance across all Commerce channels, while respecting scenarios that require operational exceptions.

Business Value:

Credit limit management is essential for business-to-business (B2B) organizations because most transactions occur on accounts, often involving large orders, long fulfillment cycles, and repeat purchasing. By enforcing well‑defined credit limits and blocking rules, your organization can control financial risk, prevent bad debt, and maintain healthy cash flow, ensuring that open orders, uninvoiced orders, and outstanding balances are all factored into a buyer’s available credit.

Before this feature enhancement, unlike Supply Chain Management orders, Commerce orders didn't follow the standard credit management capabilities. This resulted in different order processing flows that required customization to make order processing consistent.

This feature ensures consistent credit policies for customers using both Supply Chain Management and Commerce orders, reducing operational complexity and eliminating costly customizations.

title: Dynamics 365 Commerce: Omnichannel commerce - Streamline mass price updates using attribute-based pricing
description:
This feature enhancement introduces mass price update capabilities that use price attribute combinations and rule-based markups to provide an efficient way to manage large-scale pricing changes.

Pricing managers can now define pricing updates based on price attribute combinations such as product attributes, customer segments, package types, and warranty types.   • A percentage markup applied on top of a selected pricing basis, such as:
    • Current price
    • Base price
    • Inventory cost
    • Last purchase price

This functionality provides a powerful extension of category pricing logic into attribute-based pricing updates.

Automatic expiration of matching legacy pricing rules

When a new pricing rule is created using attribute combinations, the system automatically identifies existing trade agreement records that match the same targeted segments. These legacy rules can then be automatically expired, eliminating the need for pricing managers to search for and manually retire outdated entries.

Mass-update capabilities

  • Reduce repetitive data entry.
  • Lower the chance of outdated or conflicting rules.
  • Ensure cleaner pricing history and better governance.

This functionality is especially valuable for organizations managing thousands of SKUs across multiple channels.

Business Value:

Pricing managers must manually create new trade agreement records, locate every previous version of the pricing rule across entities, and individually expire outdated entries. This creates significant operational overhead, especially for companies managing large product catalogs or complex pricing structures.

With attribute-based mass pricing updates, unified pricing management now automates these processes and reduces manual effort. Pricing managers can update prices at scale using rule-driven logic, ensure consistent pricing across similar attribute combinations, and eliminate errors caused by manual expiration of legacy rules. This results in faster pricing updates, higher data accuracy, and improved responsiveness to market or cost changes.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Financial Management - Calculate taxes for plastic and sugar
description:
Business Central introduces new capabilities in excise journals to calculate tax amounts for plastic and sugar based on legislation requirements that use weight, content, and transaction quantities as the basis for excise taxes. The new Excise Tax Type, Qty. for Excise Tax, and Excise UOM fields on the Item Card and Fixed Asset Card pages let you define material composition and the relevant quantity basis for each product or fixed asset.

For tax on plastic, Business Central calculates excise quantities by aggregating item ledger entries from purchases, positive adjustments, production output, assembly output, and fixed asset ledger entries related to an acquisition. To determine the tax basis, it multiplies the calculated quantity by the defined excise quantity.

For tax on sugar, Business Central uses Item ledger entries from sales and negative adjustments to determine the total sugar content for the reporting period. The tax basis is derived by multiplying the excise quantity per unit by the total quantity sold or consumed.

These calculations generate the core data needed to report tax on plastics and sugar, while the specific country‑level tax declaration forms remain out of scope. This provides flexibility for partners and customers to adapt the output to local submission requirements while relying on standardized, accurate calculations in Business Central.

Business Value:

Many countries are introducing plastic and sugar‑related excise taxes, and companies must calculate these amounts based on material composition and quantities used or sold. Business Central provides a built‑in framework to calculate taxes on plastic and sugar without relying on manual spreadsheets or external tools. Support for these tax calculations helps organizations improve accuracy, reduce compliance risks, and prepare the core data needed for local tax declarations.

title: Dynamics 365 Commerce: Store Commerce - Enable contextual switching with external apps in POS
description:
How it works:

  1. POS to external application: A sales associate is working in POS and needs to use an external system (for example, a specialized parts-search tool). They trigger the Open URL POS operation, which opens the external application.
  2. External application back to POS: After the associate completes their task in the external system (for example, selects a part), the external application calls POS back with the relevant context—for example, a product ID and quantity. POS receives this context and navigates to the correct screen with the information loaded.
  3. Custom context handling: Businesses can add custom logic in POS to determine how incoming context from their external application is interpreted and handled.

Availability

Application: Point of sale (POS)

Setup and configuration

No additional configuration is required in Commerce headquarters or POS. However, to use this feature, the business's IT team must:

  • Customize the external application to call POS with the appropriate context parameters.
  • Optionally, add custom logic within POS to interpret and act on the context passed by the external application.

This is a developer-level customization, not an admin or store manager task.

Business Value:

Retailers and B2B commerce businesses often rely on specialized external systems such as parts-lookup tools, warranty platforms, or industry-specific catalogs alongside their point of sale (POS). Today, integrating these systems with POS requires significant development effort, and sales associates must manually re-enter information (such as product details or customer data) when moving between applications. This is time-consuming, error-prone, and costly.

Contextual switching eliminates these friction points. By enabling external applications to pass context directly into POS, businesses can drastically reduce integration time and cost. Sales associates benefit from a streamlined workflow where product, customer, and transaction context flow automatically between systems to remove the need for manual data entry. This leads to faster transactions, fewer errors, and better experiences for store employees and customers.

For businesses that depend on external tools as part of their sales process, this feature unlocks a flexible, low-friction way to extend POS without replacing existing investments in specialized systems.

  • Generate recommendations and next-best actions based on available business context.

If you spend the day moving between CRM, email, meetings, calendars, and collaboration tools, Dynamics 365 Sales skills bring that context together in Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork. By grounding Cowork in Dynamics 365 Sales data and Microsoft 365 signals, you get more relevant insights, recommendations, and actions in the flow of work. This helps you quickly understand customer relationships, opportunity health, pipeline changes, and next steps, so you spend less time gathering information and more time moving deals forward.

title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Workforce engagement management - Create capacity plans for planning groups
description:
This feature provides the following capabilities:

  • When creating or editing a capacity plan, planners can select a Planning group.
  • A capacity plan created from a forecast scenario automatically inherits the scenario’s planning group. This behavior keeps the forecast scenario and capacity plan aligned without requiring additional input.
  • For a capacity plan created from an uploaded forecast file, planners can select the planning group manually.
  • The capacity plan calculates staffing requirements from the combined demand of the queues and channels in the planning group instead of providing separate results for each queue.
  • The capacity plan list includes a Planning group column that planners can use to sort and filter plans.
  • Capacity plans created without a planning group continue to work as before.

Access and prerequisites
To use Workforce Management capabilities, an administrator must install the Workforce Management for Customer Service package from the Power Platform admin center.

Business Value:

Staffing decisions should focus on the entire team, not individual queues. Typically, one pool of representatives supports multiple queues and channels, but traditional capacity planning treats each queue separately. This creates multiple FTE estimates that planners must manually combine, often inflating requirements because shared staffing efficiencies are ignored.

With planning group support, you can manage capacity for the whole group as one unit. A single plan covers all queues, so FTE, shrinkage, and service goals are based on the combined demand your team actually handles. This approach gives you accurate staffing needs and real cost efficiency instead of overstated totals from isolated queue calculations.

Enabled for:

Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Workforce engagement management - Associate forecast scenarios with planning groups
description:
This feature provides the following capabilities:

  • When creating or editing a forecast scenario, forecasters can optionally select a planning group.
  • When a planning group is selected, the Timezone, Channel, and Queue values are populated from the planning group definition and become read-only. This behavior keeps the scenario aligned with its planning group.
  • When no planning group is selected, forecasters can manually edit the Timezone, Channel, and Queue values. Existing scenario creation workflows remain unchanged.
  • The forecast scenario list includes a Planning group column that forecasters can use to sort and filter scenarios.
  • Capacity plans created from a forecast scenario inherit the scenario’s planning group. For a capacity plan created from an uploaded file, forecasters can select the planning group manually.

Access and prerequisites

To use Workforce Management capabilities, an administrator must install the Workforce Management for Customer Service package from the Power Platform admin center.

Business Value:

Contact center demand rarely aligns perfectly with a single queue. Most lines of business, sites, or skill pools rely on multiple queues and channels that share the same agents and service goals.

Planning group support brings these queues and channels together so you can forecast them as one unit. Instead of juggling separate scenarios, you work with a single view where volume and average handle time reflect the actual demand pool your team staffs. This means you can pass accurate numbers straight to capacity planning and scheduling without extra steps. You save time, reduce errors, and measure performance at the level your business truly operates.

If you manage dozens of queues across multiple lines of business, this feature shifts forecasting from a queue-by-queue task to planning at the scale of your entire operation.

title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Workforce engagement management - Filter the adherence tracker by planning group
description:
This feature provides the following capabilities:

  • The adherence tracker includes a planning group filter that supervisors can use to scope the view to a specific planning group.
  • The planning group filter works with the existing shift plan and service representative filters, so supervisors can combine filters to refine a single view.
  • The tracker displays representatives based on the planning groups associated with their scheduled shifts. This behavior keeps the tracker aligned with the shift plan used to calculate adherence.
  • The tracker saves each supervisor’s filter selections across sessions and opens with their previous scope.
  • The tracker recalculates adherence percentages and out-of-adherence counts for the filtered scope, providing a planning group-level view of intraday adherence.
  • In Copilot Service workspace, go to Workforce management > Adherence tracker.

Access and prerequisites

To use Workforce Management capabilities, an administrator must install the Workforce Management for Customer Service package from the Power Platform admin center.

Business Value:

Supervising large contact centers is tough when you have to scan endless lists to find your team. Now, with planning group support, you can filter the adherence tracker to just the groups you manage. That means you spot issues faster and act right away, keeping service levels on track in real time instead of fixing problems after the fact. This feature scales for enterprise operations with hundreds of representatives and aligns with the same planning group structure you already use for forecasting, staffing, and scheduling. It saves time, reduces complexity, and helps you stay focused on what matters most: delivering consistent service.

title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Workforce engagement management - Filter adherence historical analytics by planning group
description:

  • The planning group filter works with the report’s existing filters, allowing managers to combine planning groups, date ranges, and other report parameters in a single view.
  • The report recalculates adherence metrics for the filtered scope, providing a group-level view of adherence performance instead of a contact center-wide aggregate.
  • The report associates representatives with planning groups through their scheduled shifts. This behavior keeps historical reporting aligned with the shift plans used to calculate adherence.
  • Planning groups must be configured and have assigned representatives before the filter returns results.

Access and prerequisites

Adherence only matters when it reflects how your work is organized. Until now, historical adherence reports didn’t account for planning groups, making it hard to see if performance dips came from a single under-supported queue or were spread across the operation.

With planning group support, you can focus your analysis on the groups that matter and compare adherence across them for the same time period. This gives you clearer insights and helps you make smarter staffing decisions.

title: Dynamics 365 Project Operations: Optimize Project Operations - Copy externally scheduled projects
description:

As part of the enhanced copy experience, you can also review and update key project attributes before completing the copy operation, including fields such as Contracting Unit, Owning Company, Calendar Template, and other project-specific settings. If you work with external scheduling tools, you can now skip the hassle of starting over. This update lets you copy those projects directly into Microsoft Dataverse, so creating a new project is quick and simple. You save time, cut down on manual work, and keep your team focused on delivering results instead of repeating tasks.

title: Power Automate: Process mining - Create and visualize custom KPIs in the process intelligence experience
description:
The process intelligence experience allows flexible metric creation with seamless visualization integration. This feature enables you to define custom KPIs and metrics tailored to specific business requirements within the process intelligence experience. You can create custom metrics using configurable formulas that can incorporate existing process data, standard KPIs, and mathematical operations.

Key capabilities include:

  • Custom metric creation: Build new KPIs using an intuitive formula editor that supports calculations based on case attributes, event data, timestamps, and existing metrics.
  • Editing and management: Modify, refine, or delete custom metrics as business needs evolve, with changes automatically reflected across all visualizations using those metrics.
  • Native visualization support: Integrate custom KPIs seamlessly into all process intelligence experience tiles and components. Display them in process maps, trend charts, statistical breakdowns, and comparative analyses just like standard metrics.
  • Business-specific measurements: Define metrics that reflect your unique business context, such as weighted performance scores, custom cost calculations, compliance rates, or domain-specific efficiency ratios.
  • Reusability: Reuse custom KPIs throughout the process intelligence experience, applying them to filters and analysis scenarios.

Custom metrics are evaluated dynamically against your process data, ensuring calculations remain current with each data refresh and providing consistent measurement across your process intelligence environment.

Business Value:

Custom KPIs put your unique business priorities at the center of process analysis. While standard metrics provide valuable baseline insights, your competitive advantage often lies in tracking the specific measurements that drive your business, whether that's customer-specific SLAs, industry-specific compliance thresholds, or proprietary efficiency calculations. This feature enables your teams to define, calculate, and monitor the exact metrics that align with your strategic goals, without waiting for IT or vendor support. Business users gain autonomy to evolve their measurement framework as priorities shift, ensuring your process intelligence always reflects current objectives. The results are more relevant insights, stronger alignment between process performance and business outcomes, and the ability to demonstrate value in the language your stakeholders understand.

title: Power Automate: Process mining - Analyze processes using object-centric process mining
description:
Real business processes rarely flow as a single, linear instance. Events routinely touch several objects of different types at the same time (for example, creating an invoice for a specific order, or shipping a package that contains items from multiple orders). Object-centric process mining captures that reality by recording events that relate to many objects and object types in one process, preserving their relationships end‑to‑end.

Here's the key idea: Instead of “one case → one sequence of activities,” object-centric process mining lets one event belong to multiple objects (and object types), keeping the full context intact.

Object-centric process mining support in Power Automate Process Mining allows you to:

  • Easily ingest your object-centric event logs from Azure Data Lake or OneLake.
  • Map object and event-level attributes to unlock detailed analytical opportunities.
  • Visualize your object-centric process in an understandable, customizable, and easy-to-read process map.
  • Visualize key metrics in a comprehensive process overview.
  • Analyze your process from process execution and throughput time viewpoint.
  • Focus on specific process areas by using filters or by specifying a particular path in the Process Analysis widget.

This premium feature is automatically enabled for all Power Automate Process Mining customers.

Business Value:

Object-centric process mining delivers transformative insights that traditional process analysis simply can't capture. By analyzing how multiple object types, such as orders, items, deliveries, and invoices interact throughout your processes, you gain a complete, realistic view of your operations as they actually function.

This comprehensive visibility enables you to identify hidden inefficiencies, such as bottlenecks that only appear when certain object combinations occur, or resource constraints that emerge from complex object interactions. You can pinpoint exactly where delays cascade across related objects, causing ripple effects that impact customer satisfaction and operational costs. The ability to analyze multiple dimensions simultaneously means faster root cause analysis and more accurate process optimization. Instead of piecing together fragmented views from separate analyses, you see the full picture immediately, reducing investigation time from weeks to hours and enabling data-driven decisions with confidence.

Ultimately, object-centric process mining helps you reduce cycle times, lower operational costs, improve resource utilization, and enhance customer experience by addressing the real complexity of your business processes rather than oversimplified approximations.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Financial Management - Use self-billed invoices
description:
Business Central offers full support for self‑billed invoices in the purchase process. Buyers can now generate invoices on behalf of a vendor when a self‑billing agreement is in place. Self‑billing reduces operational friction by allowing buyers to generate invoices on behalf of suppliers under a mutual agreement. This improves accuracy, accelerates processing, and eliminates delays caused by missing or inconsistent supplier‑issued invoices. With automated layouts, posting rules, and vendor configuration, you can streamline both compliance and internal controls while ensuring clean financial records.

title: Dynamics 365 Project Operations: Optimize Project Operations - Enable flexibility when determining financial dimension defaults
description:
Previously, you had limited options for how financial dimensions default. This feature adds functionality and flexibility to default financial dimension values. With this feature, you can:

  • Create a configuration to determine how financial dimensions default based on criteria like contract, project, or cost and revenue profile.
  • Set criteria to determine whether dimensions default from contract lines or projects.
  • Improve reliability when you save financial dimensions and value defaults on the project.
  • Add the ability to set dimensions on time and material contract lines.
  • Add the ability to use contract lines for revenue recognition.

For example, the system uses the following logic:

  • The line at the end of the grid defaults all projects and contracts to use the project dimension unless an individual record overrides that behavior.
  • The table line at the top of the grid is the next most specific record. It causes all projects associated with contract 00000017 to use the dimensions from the project line.
  • The middle line is the most specific record. It's project-specific. It overrides previously defined behavior. All transactions for Project 000000004 use the contract line for the basis of default dimensions.

The Enable contract line based revenue recognition with Project Operations for non-stocked/resource based scenarios feature modifies the Project default dimension rules form by adding a column to add rules based on specific contract line groups as the first filter.

title: Dynamics 365 Project Operations: Notify users when approval sets finish processing

title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: Workforce engagement management - Automate shift rotations for consistent workforce coverage
description:
What the feature does

Shift rotation policies help organizations distribute customer service representatives across recurring shifts on a configurable schedule. Supervisors can create rotation policies that define how representatives move between time slots over time and apply those policies to shift plans.

Supervisors create policies by specifying a start date, time zone, rotation cadence, and a set of recurring time slots. Representatives are assigned to each time slot, and the scheduler automatically applies the rotation pattern when generating future schedules. This reduces the need for manual shift reassignment while supporting consistent workforce coverage across operating hours.

Changes to a policy affect only future scheduling runs. Existing bookings remain unchanged. When additional staffing is needed, the scheduler can use available flexible workers or other eligible representatives who can cover the required time period.

How the feature is enabled

Administrators enable Workforce Management and shift scheduling capabilities in Customer Service. Supervisors then create and manage shift rotation policies, assign representatives to rotation groups, and associate policies with shift plans.

After a policy is assigned to a shift plan, future automatic scheduling runs apply the configured rotation pattern. Supervisors can pause a policy or remove it from a shift plan at any time to stop rotation-based scheduling.

Business Value:

Organizations that operate 24/7 contact centers or use rotating shifts can reduce the time supervisors spend manually reassigning agents to schedules. With shift rotation policies, administrators define the rotation pattern once and the scheduler automatically applies it. This helps ensure fair and predictable shift distribution for customer service representatives, reduces administrative overhead for supervisors, and supports consistent staffing coverage across operating hours.

title: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Journeys: Elevate customer experiences - Automatically update emails with the latest content
description:
By automatically updating emails with latest content, you can:

  • Easily create dynamic content blocks in Content gallery with new content or select existing content in email and save it as a dynamic content block.
  • Have content only so it uses the layout of the email when inserted or have content with its layout preserved. You can mark the content block as “protected” to prevent content from being modified in the email.
  • Allow personalized content (for example, dynamic text or conditional content).
  • Easily see which emails will be updated when you update such content blocks.

Dynamic content blocks can be enabled by going to the Settings > Feature switches area and turning on the feature switch Dynamic content block.

Imagine a financial service company that includes a standard footer in each email that has legal disclaimer text along with a blurb about their company that includes assets under management and recent accolades and awards. Given the sensitivity of legal text, and the fact that key information about their company (assets under management) change every few months, they find it hard and inefficient to manually update all emails in use across multiple campaigns. Customer trust is eroded if the same customer receives two emails with different information about their company, or worse, an old legal disclaimer text.

Such issues can now be avoided with dynamic content blocks. The marketing team can now put such regularly updated content in a dynamic content block included in the footer (you can do this as part of the email template itself). Now when this content block is updated, every email that includes the content block is automatically updated, ensuring customers receive the most recent content.

Dynamic content blocks can include personalized content to make emails more engaging. For example, the content block can include conditional content and dynamic text to include only the most relevant awards for the customer’s industry or financial level.

Business Value:

No business can afford to appear unprofessional or lower trust in their brand by sending emails with outdated or inaccurate information. Stakes are much higher with legal and disclaimer text routinely included in every email (usually via the footer). Updating such content in every email can be very time-consuming and error-prone.

Dynamic content blocks eliminate such manual work and the risk of sending emails with outdated content. When a dynamic content block is updated, all emails using that block are automatically refreshed to ensure recipients always receive the most current content.

This feature simplifies access management through Microsoft Entra security groups. Administrators assign roles to a group once. They grant or revoke access instantly by adding or removing users from the groups.

Organizations reduce administrative burden, strengthen access control, and speed up onboarding. New service representatives receive the access they need on day one. title: Dynamics 365 Finance: Core financials - Detect corruption in source document budget control tracking
description:

These conditions can make it harder for finance users to understand why budget control data does not reconcile as expected and where repair should begin. With this feature, Dynamics 365 Finance adds diagnostic capability to Budget control data maintenance. The diagnostic is designed to detect corrupted budget tracking data patterns before users run repair actions and highlight budget-controlled documents that are affected by orphaned budget tracking records, where the underlying budget source is missing. It also identifies broken relieving relationships between commitments and relieving documents, helping users understand where budget tracking data requires attention.
This capability complements source document reprocessing. Finance users can first run the diagnostic to detect corruption and understand the affected documents, then use the existing budget control data maintenance tool to repair the data.

By highlighting budget-controlled documents affected by orphaned tracking records or broken relieving relationships, the diagnostic gives users a clearer starting point for analysis and remediation. title: Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management: Manufacturing and asset management - Enforce same-batch selection for raw materials in production and batch orders
description:
This feature ensures that raw materials consumed by production orders and batch orders all come from the same batch. Process and discrete manufacturers can use it together with related production-control capabilities that govern how raw materials are allocated to a production order.

Product designers and production engineers can set the same-batch requirement at the released-product level so that it applies by default everywhere the item is consumed. They can optionally fine-tune it for individual bill of materials (BOM) or formula lines where a different rule is appropriate. Production planners and warehouse workers who reserve raw materials for a production or batch order see the system automatically restrict the available on-hand inventory to a single batch per line, instead of mixing quantities from several batches. The result is the consistent, traceable, single-batch consumption pattern that's needed for quality-controlled manufacturing scenarios—without requiring operators to remember and enforce the rule manually.

Key capabilities available in Supply Chain Management version 10.0.49

Version 10.0.49 of Supply Chain Management introduces the following capabilities to support same-batch selection for raw materials in production and batch orders:

  • Configure same-batch selection at the product level as a default requirement to ensure consistent raw material consumption.
  • Allow overrides on formula and BOM lines to support flexibility where batch consistency requirements differ.
  • Enforce same-batch reservation by ensuring raw material reservation respects the same-batch requirement defined on formula and BOM lines.
  • Support traceability and control by preventing mixed-batch consumption during raw material reservation.

Enhancements planned for future versions of Supply Chain Management

Future versions of Supply Chain Management are expected to introduce additional capabilities to further enhance same-batch selection for raw materials in production and batch orders, including:

  • Same-batch enforcement during master planning allocation.
  • Execution validation to ensure that same-batch requirements are validated during picking and consumption for production.

Business Value:

Same-batch selection helps ensure consistent product quality and traceability by preventing mixed-batch consumption, reducing compliance risk, and simplifying production control.

title: Dynamics 365 Finance: Globalization Studio - Enhance Electronic Reporting with new capabilities
description:
Electronic Reporting (ER) is the configurable engine you use to author and run business documents—invoices, statutory reports, VAT declarations and payment files, and more. In 10.0.48 and 10.0.49 Microsoft delivered a set of general enhancements that respond directly to the most highly voted ideas on the Microsoft Idea portal and to recurring partner/customer requests. The enhancements remove long-standing workarounds, expand what ER formats can express out of the box, and modernize commonly used destinations.

You can now:

  • Send generated documents to silent (BCC) recipients straight from ER.
  • Produce industry-standard GS1 barcodes directly in your ER labels.
  • Write cleaner ER formulas using new integer-arithmetic functions.
  • Print the exact number of copies you configured for ER-based documents.
  • Run validation for multiple ER configurations at scale, with background execution and full traceability of validation results across configuration versions.
  • Run ER with improved memory efficiency, enabling more reliable processing of large-volume reports and complex datasets.

New capabilities

Send blind copies (BCC) from ER Email destinations

With this release wave, the ER Email destination is extended with support for blind carbon copy (BCC) recipients. In previous versions, only To and Cc recipients could be configured, which limited the ability to distribute generated documents to compliance, audit, or archival mailboxes without disclosing those addresses to the primary recipients.

ER's Email destination now includes a Bcc field next to To and Cc.

  • To enable, select Electronic reporting > Electronic reporting destination > File destination > Settings > Email.
  • The Bcc field accepts the same kinds of values as To and Cc: static addresses, ER expressions, or values bound to the data model.

Business outcome: Confidential distribution of ER-generated documents to compliance, audit, and archival mailboxes is achieved entirely through configuration, eliminating the need for customization or post-processing.

Generate GS1 barcodes directly from ER

GS1 is the global standard for barcodes used in retail, warehousing, supply chain, transportation, and healthcare.

ER now generates GS1 barcodes natively, with three new formats available in the barcode data source:

  • GS1-128
  • GS1 DataMatrix
  • GS1 QR Code

When you choose one of these formats, ER applies the correct GS1 encoding rules automatically. ER also warns you at design time when the configured barcode width is too small to scan reliably, so you catch problems before they reach the shop floor.

Business outcome: You can design GS1-compliant labels (warehouse, shipping, retail, healthcare) entirely inside ER, with no third-party barcode tools.

New ER formula functions: DIV and MOD

Integer division and remainder are common in reporting—for pagination, packaging quantities, currency splits, period bucketing, and check-digit calculations. Previously, ER report authors had to express these with combinations of ROUND, subtraction, and multiplication, which is verbose and easy to get wrong.

Two new functions are now part of the ER formula language:

  • DIV(a, b) — integer division. Returns the integer (or Int64) quotient.
  • MOD(a, b) — the remainder of integer division. Returns the integer (or Int64) remainder.

Business outcome: Cleaner, faster, and more readable ER formulas wherever whole-number arithmetic is needed.

ER destinations now apply the configured number of copies in Print management

When an ER-based document—for example, Container content—was configured in Print management with a number of copies greater than one, the printer still produced only a single copy. Warehouse, manufacturing, and logistics teams had to duplicate documents manually, slowing down pick, pack, and ship operations.

ER destinations now correctly print the Number of copies configured in Print management, as well as the number requested in ad-hoc print dialogs. This applies across the standard entry points for ER documents driven by Print management.

Business outcome: The number of copies you configure is the number of copies you get—faster throughput, and fewer process errors.

Optimize memory consumption for large Electronic Reporting (ER) executions

This feature enhances memory efficiency during Electronic Reporting execution by introducing targeted optimizations in the reporting engine. These improvements reduce peak memory consumption by minimizing unnecessary object creation, avoiding redundant data duplication in memory, and reusing existing data structures more effectively.

The optimization is broadly applicable across Electronic Reporting scenarios and is particularly beneficial for reports that process large volumes of data. Because the improvements are built into the engine, you benefit from them automatically, no configuration changes or report redesign are required.

Business outcome: Large ER reports run more reliably with reduced peak memory usage, lowering the risk of out-of-memory failures and helping high-volume reporting workloads complete consistently.

Enhanced validation management for Electronic Reporting configurations

This feature enables validation of multiple Electronic Reporting (ER) configuration versions in a single operation. When the feature is enabled, the Configuration repository page introduces a Validation experience that lets you:

  • Select and validate multiple completed ER configurations at once, instead of validating one version at a time.
  • Run validation as a batch job, so large validation workloads no longer block interactive sessions.
  • Review validation results through a persistent Validation history, where results are retained for later review by configuration and version.

This feature also introduces version-level validation tracking. Both users and system processes can identify which configuration versions have already been validated in the current environment, which helps you avoid redundant validation runs and focus on versions that still need attention.

Business outcome: Configuration quality can be governed at scale—teams validate many configuration versions in a single batch operation and rely on a persistent history and version-level tracking to confirm what has already been validated, reducing manual effort and rework.

Instead of keeping process analytics isolated in a standalone tool, your teams can now blend object-centric process metrics with financial data, operational KPIs, customer information, and other enterprise data sources within Fabric's unified platform. title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Copilot and AI innovation - Resolve customer emails autonomously with AI
description:

Using enterprise knowledge, configured business instructions, connectors, and custom agents, the system constructs a resolution dynamically. If the customer isn't satisfied or the issue can't be resolved automatically, the system creates a case that carries the full conversation context, including customer intent, actions taken, and generated responses. A service representative can then step in without losing context or duplicating work.

The capability is delivered through the Case Management Agent. An administrator enables the setting and sets the automation level for each line of business, from fully autonomous resolution to drafting a response for a service representative to review and send.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Copilot and agents - Run multiple Sales Order Agents per company with smarter item matching, relevance filtering, and streamlined setup
description:
You can now configure and run multiple Sales Order Agent instances in a single company. Each instance operates independently with its own mailbox, folder settings, email signature, and processing rules.

Each agent instance tracks its own KPI metrics, such as emails received, quotes created, orders created, and time saved. The setup page is restructured to support per-instance configuration, and an upgrade path migrates existing single-instance setups to the new architecture. This change allows organizations to set up separate agents for different sales teams, product lines, or customer segments, each monitoring their own personal or shared mailbox.

Improved items search:

When a customer requests items, the agent now uses a multi-layer matching strategy:

  • Exact identifier match: direct lookup by item number, vendor item number, GTIN, or cross-reference.
  • Semantic attribute matching: extracts attributes from the customer's message (color, material, size) and ranks candidates by relevance using AI.
  • Broader fuzzy search: falls back to a global item search when direct and attribute-based searches produce no results.

Message and attachment relevance:

The agent now validates incoming messages and attachments against a detailed relevance model before processing. Messages that fall outside the agent's responsibilities (such as offers to sell, requests for discounts, or attempts to extract internal information) are identified and filtered.

A separate relevance check runs on attachments, ensuring that non-sales-related documents don't trigger unnecessary processing. The validation considers the full conversation history and the agent's defined scope to make accurate relevance decisions.

Larger attachment files with diagnostics.

The maximum number of pages per PDF attachment has been raised from 10 to 50, addressing customer feedback about the agent not reading larger purchase orders. A new cumulative content length limit of 150,000 characters is also enforced across all attachments in a single email (approximately 50K tokens).

When an attachment is skipped, Business Central now stores the specific reason directly on the attachment record (page count exceeded, cumulative content length exceeded, attachment count exceeded, unsupported format, or analyze-attachments not enabled). This information is visible on the Attachments page and logged in telemetry, making it straightforward to diagnose why a particular document wasn't processed.

Try it out.

You can now create tasks for the Sales Order Agent without sending an email. From the agent's setup page, a new Try it out section lets you compose a message by selecting a sender (from your contact or customer list), entering message text, and attaching files. The agent acts like it received a real email.

To help you get started quickly, two sample messages are included. One is a text-only message that references items from your catalog, and the other is a message with a sample purchase order attachment. The sample order is generated based on your actual item data, so the agent has realistic content to work with.

These samples are particularly useful for first-time setup, demos, and testing agent behavior with specific scenarios without needing to send an actual email.

Handling of unknown senders

When the agent receives an email from an unregistered email address, you now have three options instead of just one:

  • Create a new contact: register the sender as a new contact (existing behavior)
  • Use another contact once: pick an existing contact from the contact list and link them to this specific task only, without modifying any master data. The override is stored per task message and does not affect future emails.
  • Update an existing contact's email: select an existing contact and update their email address to the sender's address

More control over email

New configuration options give administrators more control over how the agent interacts with the monitored mailbox:

  • Mark email as read: a new toggle to mark processed emails as read in the mailbox. This works in addition to the custom Processed by Sales Order Agent category, giving users a visual signal in their inbox.
  • Mandatory folder selection: the agent now requires you to select a specific mailbox folder before activation. Previously this was optional and could lead to the agent monitoring an unexpected folder. If in doubt, choose Inbox.
  • Stricter activation validation: trying to activate the agent without a mailbox folder now shows a clear error message instead of allowing activation in an ambiguous state.

Prompts as embedded resources.

The agent's AI prompts (instructions, item search logic, mail template checks, irrelevance validation) are now shipped as embedded resource files within the app extension package. This change reduces latency on first task processing and makes the prompt structure more transparent for engineering iteration.

Business Value:

The Sales Order Agent now handles more complex organizational structures and higher volumes with less manual intervention. You can run multiple agent instances in one company, each dedicated to a different team or shared mailbox with independent settings and performance tracking. The agent finds the right items more reliably by understanding product attributes, informal descriptions, and identifiers across multiple matching layers.
The agent now processes PDFs up to 50 pages (previously, the limit was 10) and clearly shows why any attachment was skipped. It also filters irrelevant messages before processing, so credits aren't consumed by marketing emails or out-of-scope inquiries. If a customer writes from an unregistered email address, you can link an existing contact to that single task without creating duplicates. You can test the agent directly from the setup page without sending a real email, reducing the time to validate your configuration.

title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Workforce engagement management - Manage policy strictness to enforce governance policies
description:
This feature introduces policy strictness control, enabling organizations to define how rigorously each governance policy evaluates and flags potential violations in outgoing emails. Governance policies serve as real-time guardrails, ensuring communications adhere to business, legal, and compliance standards before they are sent to customers.

With this enhancement, supervisors can configure the strictness level for each policy. Lower strictness settings apply more lenient enforcement, reducing false positives and allowing borderline scenarios to pass, while higher settings perform more rigorous checks to identify subtle or potentially risky violations. This flexibility allows organizations to align policy enforcement with their compliance requirements and risk tolerance.

All policies are set to medium strictness by default, providing a balanced level of enforcement. Organizations can then adjust strictness levels per policy depending on the nature of the rule. For example, highly sensitive policies, such as those related to data protection or regulatory compliance, can be configured with stricter enforcement, while policies focused on tone or content guidance can be set to be more lenient to avoid unnecessary disruptions.

At runtime, the governance policies use the configured strictness level to determine how policy violations are flagged when outgoing emails are evaluated. This ensures that enforcement is consistent and adaptable across different policy types and business scenarios.

By enabling strictness control at the policy level, organizations can fine-tune governance enforcement without modifying the underlying policy definitions, helping balance compliance protection, agent productivity, and a seamless customer communication experience.

Business Value:

Take control of how your governance policies handle outbound email violations. With adjustable strictness levels, you can cut down on false positives when flexibility matters or apply tighter controls for sensitive situations. This balance helps you build confidence in AI-driven enforcement while keeping your policies aligned with your risk tolerance, compliance requirements, and business goals.

title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Workforce engagement management - Enforce governance policies on email attachments
description:
This feature extends governance capabilities to evaluate email attachments, closing a critical gap where sensitive or non-compliant information may exist outside the email body.

When a user sends an email with attachments, the system automatically scans each document and applies configured governance policies. In the initial release, analysis is focused on plain text content within supported document types, such as Word and PDF files. Non-text elements, including images or embedded content, are excluded in this phase to ensure predictable and efficient processing.

Every attachment included in an email is evaluated individually, and all applicable policies are enforced across each file. If multiple attachments are present, governance policies check all of them, ensuring that no document bypasses validation. If even a single attachment violates a configured policy, such as containing restricted content or failing compliance rules, the entire email is blocked from being sent.

Administrators can configure policies to explicitly include attachment checks during policy setup. This allows organizations to apply governance selectively based on business needs, such as enforcing stricter controls for sensitive communications while maintaining flexibility for general scenarios. Existing policies can be updated to enable attachment analysis, while new policies can be configured to include attachments by default where required.

To ensure transparency and accountability, all attachment evaluations are logged, including details such as which attachment triggered a violation and the reason for failure. Users are provided with clear feedback when an email is blocked, helping them quickly identify and correct issues before resending. This improves user experience while maintaining strong governance controls.

Business Value:

You can now apply governance controls to email attachments, not just the message body. This helps you stop sensitive or non-compliant content from being sent externally. By scanning attachment text, you catch policy issues early and block risky emails before they go out. That means stronger compliance, less data leakage, and consistent protection across every outbound channel.

title: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Session and Response Sharing in M365 Copilot
description: Session and Response Sharing let Microsoft 365 Copilot users share Copilot chat content through a link. Session Sharing shares a full chat session, while Response Sharing shares a single Copilot response. The shared content opens as a read-only view, and recipients can continue from it in their own Copilot chat. This gives Copilot users an easier and more controlled way to share useful Copilot outputs with coworkers instead of copying and pasting. It helps teams reuse work, share context, and collaborate more efficiently while keeping sharing within organizational controls.
